# **UREC 1 RESEARCH ETHICS REVIEW FOR STUDENT RESEARCH WITH NO HUMAN PARTICIPANTS OR DIRECT COLLECTION OF HUMAN TISSUES, OR BODILY FLUIDS.**

All University research is required to undergo ethical scrutiny to comply with UK law. The University Research Ethics Policy ([www.shu.ac.uk/research/excellence/ethics-and-integrity/policies](https://www.shu.ac.uk/research/excellence/ethics-and-integrity/policies)) should be consulted before completing this form. The initial questions are there to check that completion of the UREC1 is appropriate for this study. The supervisor will approve the study, but it may also be reviewed by the College Teaching Program Research Ethics Committee (CTPREC) as part of the quality assurance process (additional guidance can be obtained from your College Research Ethics Chair<sup><sup>[\[1\]](#footnote-1)</sup></sup>).

The final responsibility for ensuring that ethical research practices are followed rests with the supervisor for student research.

Note that students and staff are responsible for making suitable arrangements to ensure compliance with the General Data Protection Regulations (GDPR), for keeping data secure and if relevant, for keeping the identity of participants anonymous. They are also responsible for following SHU guidelines about data encryption and research data management. Guidance can be found on the SHU Ethics Website [www.shu.ac.uk/research/excellence/ethics-and-integrity](https://www.shu.ac.uk/research/excellence/ethics-and-integrity)

Please note that it is mandatory for all students to only store data on their allotted networked F drive space and not on individual hard drives or memory sticks etc.

This form also enables the University and College to keep a record confirming that research conducted has been subjected to ethical scrutiny. Students should retain a copy for inclusion in their research projects, and a copy should be uploaded to the relevant module Blackboard site.

The form must be completed by the student and approved by the supervisor and/or module leader (as applicable). In all cases, it should be counter-signed by the supervisor and/or module leader and kept as a record showing that ethical scrutiny has occurred. Students should retain a copy for inclusion in the appendices of their research projects, and a copy should be uploaded to the module Blackboard site for checking.

Please note that it may be necessary to conduct a health and safety risk assessment for the proposed research. Further information can be obtained from the University's Health and Safety Website <https://sheffieldhallam.sharepoint.com/sites/3069/SitePages/Risk-Assessment.aspx>

| Brief outline of research to include, rationale (reasons) for undertaking the research & aims, and methods (max 500 words). | This research project significantly analyses the utilisation of Artificial Intelligence and machine learning techniques for improving cyber security threat Detection system. The increasing number of Cyber-attacks such as Malware, phishing, denial of service attacks and network intrusions has created a demand for more intelligent and adaptive cyber security solutions. Moreover, the traditional rule-based detection system mainly struggles to identify new and dynamic threats, making AI driven approaches increasingly significant in the modern cybersecurity environment.<br><br>The aim of this research is to evaluate the effectiveness of machine learning algorithms in detecting cyber security threats using publicly available intrusion detection datasets. The study also concentrated on supervised machine learning algorithms such as random forest, logistics regression and XGBoost to compare their accuracy, recall and efficiency in the case of identifying malicious networks activities. The research also analysed how datasets quality, class imbalance, and feature engineering impacted the performance of models.<br><br>The Metrology will include collecting secondary information from publicly available information such as NSL-KDD and CICIDS2017. The data processing techniques such as normalisation, feature selection and balancing method will be implemented before training and models. This model will be evaluated by using standard performance Matrix to determine which algorithm provides the best balance between accuracy and computational efficiency.<br><br>The project does not effectively include human participation for collecting information, personal data collection, and sensitive information. Moreover, all the datasets are anonymised and publicly available for academic research purposes. The research is intended solely for defensive cybersecurity purposes and aims to contribute to the development of more intelligence and adaptive intrusion detection systems.<br><br>The research will be carried out according to Sheffield Hallam University guidelines concerning research ethics, data protection, and ethical use of artificial intelligence technologies. As there will be no participation of human beings, interviews, questionnaires, or observations in the process, there is virtually no risk of any possible violation of research ethics that might lead to potential harm done to the participants. However, the proper handling of cybersecurity-related data and results of machine learning analysis remains important.<br><br>All datasets utilised during the research will be taken from official sources - namely, acknowledged public cybersecurity databases and other scientific sources. The datasets will consist solely of anonymous data without any personal identifying information provided. No attempt will be made to determine individual identity or affiliation of entities mentioned in the datasets. Data will be used strictly for academics.<br><br>The project will also look at the ethics associated with artificial intelligence usage within cybersecurity frameworks. Even though the technology will greatly aid in detecting attacks and developing automated solutions to deal with such threats, there may be the possibility of misuse of these discoveries for carrying out cyber-attacks. For this reason, the research will be completely focused on defensive cybersecurity purposes only, without publishing any information regarding attacks or weaknesses found.<br><br>All project materials, whether datasets or documents related to pre-processing techniques and algorithms used during the course of the project will be safely stored using Sheffield Hallam University-approved storage platforms, including the allocated university network drive. There will be no usage of any personal storage device or any external cloud platform for storing such data. |

**Insurance Check**

The University's standard insurance cover will not automatically cover research involving any of the following:

i) Participants under 5 years old

ii) Pregnant women

iii) 5000 or more participants

iv) Research being conducted in an overseas country

v) Research involving aircraft and offshore oil rigs

vi) Nuclear research

vii) Any trials/medical research into Covid 19

If your proposals do involve any of the above, please contact the Insurance Manager directly ([fin-insurancequeries-mb@exchange.shu.ac.uk](mailto:fin-insurancequeries-mb@exchange.shu.ac.uk)) to discuss this element of your project.

| R4     | Delay in reviewing literature and conducting experiments or writing the report may result in the project being delayed.                            | Medium          | Medium     | Project Management risk | Creating a detailed schedule with buffer time                          |
| R5     | There could be bias during the evaluation of algorithms because of inconsistencies in the process.                                                 | Low             | Medium     | Research Validity Risk  | Applying the same preprocessing methods                                |
| R6     | The results obtained using artificial intelligence for cybersecurity could potentially be misused in offensive cybersecurity.                      | Low             | High       | Ethical risk            | Assuring the project remaining focused only on defensive cybersecurity |
| R7     | Dataset imbalance and bad quality of data could negatively impact the reliability of the models developed.                                         | Medium          | High       | Data Quality risk       | Using SMOTE balancing techniques                                       |
